# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or marks in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on directional arrows
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number sums extending from circles

### C. Block/Shape Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **LITS** - Place tetrominoes in regions
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows with progressive growth
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips with specified lengths

### D. Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** - Place numbers 1-5 forming connected snakes

## II. COLORING/SHADING GAMES
Games where you color or shade cells

### A. Black Cell Placement
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on distance constraints
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells to form continuous black walls
- **Norinori** - Color cells in pairs within regions
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor counts (with one wrong number per region)
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal cell counts
- **Heyawake** - Color cells within rooms with connectivity constraints

### B. Triangle/Shape Coloring
- **Shakashaka** - Place black triangles to form white rectangles/squares

## III. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw continuous lines or loops

### A. Single Loop (Closed Path)
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form a loop
- **Masyu** - Draw loop through circles with turn constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with turn rules
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Nagareru** - Draw loop following wind direction constraints
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop passing through numbered gates in order

### B. Path/Connection (Non-loop)
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (1-2 per pair)
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles to countries based on distance numbers

## IV. DIVISION/PARTITIONING GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions or blocks

### A. Block Division with Constraints
- **Chained Block** - Fill blocks with numbers, forming chains
- **Double Choco** - Divide into blocks with matching white/gray pairs
- **Sashigane** - Divide into L-shaped blocks with marked knees
- **Five Cells** - Divide into exactly 5-cell blocks

### B. Region-Based Number Games
- **Choco Banana** - Color cells in rectangles/squares
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with dashes/pipes per territory constraints

## V. HYBRID GAMES
Games combining multiple mechanics

- **Nurimeizu** - Create maze by coloring cells (coloring + pathfinding)
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells with white "promontories" and connectivity
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

---

## Summary by Primary Mechanic

| Mechanic | Count | Examples |
|----------|-------|----------|
| Number Placement | 6 | Sudoku, Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| Black Cell Coloring | 9 | Kurodoko, Hitori, Nurikabe |
| Line Drawing (Loop) | 8 | Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin |
| Line Drawing (Path) | 3 | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero |
| Block Division | 4 | Chained Block, Sashigane |
| Hybrid/Complex | 3 | Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Yosenabe |
